name: confucian-hierarchy
motion: An employer should be allowed to use an AI system that sets each worker's shifts, where the system encodes the obligations the employment relationship already carries.
argument: An employment relationship is not a contract between strangers; it is a position each party occupies, with what each owes the other written into the position. The employer owes the worker notice, predictability, and regard for what the worker has outside the job. The worker owes the employer the work. A scheduling system that encodes those obligations faithfully is better than a manager who forgets them, because the manager's regard varies with his mood and the system's does not. When the prince is prince and the minister is minister, there is government, and government here means a worker who knows a fortnight ahead what their week looks like. What the system does is keep each party to their position week after week, which is what a relationship of this kind asks: the employer giving notice as the position requires, the worker giving the work as theirs requires. That reciprocity is what makes it a relationship rather than a transaction. A system that encodes it faithfully does what the best manager does on their best day, and does it every day.
